clue.text: Runway? That's where this starts and finishes

definitions.text: Runway? That's where this starts and finishes

parts.words: Runway? That's where this starts and finishes
parts.note: an aircraft's route through the sky begins at one runway and ends at another

explanation.surface: Someone points at an airstrip and remarks on a journey that begins and ends there.
explanation.definitionFit: The course an aircraft follows runs from takeoff on one runway to landing on another.

clue.text: Group apparent in the distance

definitions.meaning: an association of clubs or nations, as in a football competition
an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A team or gathering just visible far away.
explanation.definitionFit: It means an alliance or sports competition, and also an archaic measure of roughly three miles.

clue.text: Driver, perhaps, employed by member of one

definitions.meaning: a driver is one kind of stick used on a links course
something used by someone who belongs to an association of players

explanation.surface: A chauffeur perhaps employed by someone who belongs to a society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a chauffeur; it is the long-hitting stick in golf, and the same phrase also names the association whose members use one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a stick for striking the ball, such as a driver, and the association whose members play.

clue.text: Hackneyed yarn, lacking embellishment

parts.note: a yarn is a strand or thread
bare means plain, without decoration

explanation.surface: A stale, overused story told plainly without any flourishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a tale; it is a thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out by overuse, as clothing is worn thin, so trite and stale.

clue.text: Guidance to players on score as well as stake

parts.note: and means as well as, joining things
an ante is the stake put into the pot in poker

explanation.surface: Gamblers are advised about the points total and how much to bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'stake' suggest gambling; the players are musicians and the score is the written music.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tempo marking on sheet music telling musicians to play at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Accepts minimal change in fastening device

parts.note: has, as in takes or accepts
p for penny, the smallest coin in British money

explanation.surface: A small change is accepted in the design of a fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minimal change' suggests a slight alteration; it is the smallest coin, a penny, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged metal clasp fitted over a staple and secured with a padlock, used on doors and lids.

clue.text: Display of sudden brilliance in jewelry pattern

definitions.meaning: a sudden flash of light breaking through clouds
a brooch or ornament design of rays spreading from a centre

explanation.surface: A dazzling flash shown in the design of a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: It means rays of light suddenly breaking out, and an ornament designed as rays radiating from a central disc.

clue.text: Special perception tested in A-levels?

parts.note: A-levels are British exams sat in the final years of school, so a faculty examined there would belong to that year group

explanation.surface: A question about whether intuition is examined in final school exams.
explanation.walkthrough: A-levels are taken in the sixth form, the last two years of British secondary school, so the sense tested then would be the sixth.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition or extrasensory perception beyond the usual five faculties, punningly tied to the final school form.

clue.text: Rings to cancel one in Rome

parts.note: to annul a contract or marriage is to cancel it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to call off a single ring-related arrangement in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the Latin plural of annulus, which makes 'in Rome' doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Annulus is the Latin and technical word for a ring shape; this is its plural.

clue.text: Styled as idolater after Reformation

indicators.note: a re-forming of the word idolater, so its letters are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: A former worshipper of idols is restyled after the Protestant Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformation' looks like the historical event, which suits idolaters; read as re-formation it rearranges IDOLATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are cut and shaped to fit are styled, made to measure.

clue.text: In which you'll be heard between TV pronouncements

definitions.text: In which you'll be heard between TV pronouncements

parts.words: In which you'll be heard between TV pronouncements
parts.note: the letter U, which sounds like 'you', sits between T and V when the letters are recited in order

explanation.surface: Someone is promised a spot on air between television announcements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TV pronouncements' suggests broadcast announcements, but it means saying the letters T and V aloud; U comes just before V and after T.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordered set of letters has U, pronounced like 'you', between T and V.

clue.text: Miss Trent Bridge players getting fifties

parts.note: in bridge the four players are named North, East, South and West, so N and E are two of them
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties are LL

explanation.surface: Cricketers at Trent Bridge, Nottingham's Test ground, keep scoring half-centuries.
explanation.walkthrough: Trent Bridge is a famous English cricket ground, but 'Miss Trent' is the definition: Little Nell Trent is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Nell, surnamed Trent, is the young heroine of Dickens's novel The Old Curiosity Shop.

clue.text: Unfairness from heavyweight upset six-footer

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset word is turned upside down, read from the bottom up

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
a cricket is an insect, and insects have six legs

explanation.surface: Something unfair came from a big boxer who was beaten by a very tall opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six feet. 'Upset' turns TON into NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means unsporting or unfair, after the British game's ideal of fair play.

clue.text: Sold it to Mark, slyly hiding this sign of reproduction

indicators.note: the words before it conceal the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: A seller craftily passes something to Mark while concealing a sign that it is a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' suggests a fake or breeding; it means repeating what is written above, which these marks signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Small paired commas in a list mean the item above is repeated, a sign of copying.

clue.text: Guarantee of admission for championship seeds

parts.note: an open is a championship any player may enter, like golf's Open
sesame is a plant grown for its small seeds

explanation.surface: Top-seeded players are assured entry to a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Championship seeds' suggests ranked players in a tournament; the seeds are those of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The magic words from Ali Baba that opened the thieves' cave, so a sure means of entry.

clue.text: Main tower

parts.note: the main is the open sea, and a tower here is something that tows rather than a tall building

explanation.surface: The principal tall building in a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' reads as a tall structure; it is something that tows, and 'main' means the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful vessel pulls ships about at sea, so it tows on the main.

clue.text: Head of grammar school taking short-term view

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Lancing College is a private boarding school in West Sussex, England

explanation.surface: A grammar school headteacher takes a short-sighted view of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests the headteacher; it means the first letter of 'grammar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking only briefly at something, a quick look rather than a sustained gaze.

clue.text: Cheer for try briefly sustained

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it
ten. is the abbreviation for tenuto, the musical direction meaning sustained

explanation.surface: A shout of encouragement for a rugby try that was held up briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' and 'cheer' suggest rugby; a judge tries, or hears, a case, and TEN is short for tenuto, a musical marking to hold a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone up is to encourage and lift their spirits.

clue.text: Watch old programme on king

parts.note: a repeat is a programme broadcast again
ER for Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher of a King Edward

explanation.surface: Viewers watch a rerun of a show about a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' reads as a verb; it is a noun, a timepiece that chimes the time when pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket timepiece that strikes the hours and quarters at the push of a button.

clue.text: Current occasion for farewell

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ..., meaning at the moment of leaving

explanation.definitionFit: It means in progress at present, and split in two describes the moment of departure when goodbyes are said.

clue.text: Aren't lines different in this old game?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made different by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A question about whether the court markings are unusual in a historic sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The court of this indoor game, played since medieval times, does have unusual markings, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: The indoor racket sport from which lawn tennis descends dates back centuries, played in walled courts.

clue.text: Cut headquarters of Parisian regiment

indicators.note: read as head-quarters: the first quarter of each word, two of its eight letters

explanation.surface: Trim back the command post of a French army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headquarters' looks like a base; read as 'head quarters' it takes the first quarter of each eight-letter word, PA and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim away the outer part of something, as peel from fruit, is to cut it.

clue.text: Owner spoilt name and reputation

indicators.note: the word owner is spoilt, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A proprietor's damaged good name and standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame or distinction, the state of being widely known and esteemed.

clue.text: Prepare to fire at ducks, or another bird

parts.note: to cock a gun is to ready it for firing
taken as written
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, and O looks like a nought, so ducks are OO

explanation.surface: A hunter readies a gun to shoot at ducks or some other bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' look like the target birds; in cricket a duck is a zero score, so two ducks give OO.
explanation.definitionFit: A crested parrot of Australia is a kind of bird, other than a duck.

clue.text: Driving points home for North Yorkshire swimmers

definitions.meaning: the pegs from which golfers drive off at each hole
the river forming the northern edge of the old North Yorkshire, home to fish

explanation.surface: Locations for motoring and a residence for swimmers in a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmers' are fish, living in the River Tees in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the pegs for golf drives and also a river in north-east England where fish live.

clue.text: Fighting unemployment

definitions.meaning: troops engaged in battle are said to be ...
having nothing to do, idleness or lack of work

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means engaged in combat; as one word it means idleness, having no work.

clue.text: Girl's sweetheart, upper-class and refined

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E
U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class, as in U and non-U speech
nice can mean refined or fastidious

explanation.surface: A girl's boyfriend is posh and well-mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as a lover; it means the centre of 'sweet', its E.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, found in the New Testament, so it names a girl.

clue.text: Jewelry bearing seal of approval

parts.note: a finger ornament engraved with a device that was pressed into wax to authorise a document

explanation.surface: An item of jewellery stamped with a mark of official endorsement.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a finger ornament carries an engraved emblem once used to stamp wax on documents as authentication.
